extracted.intended_audience: scientists, journal editors, peer reviewers, and authors in the life sciences
extracted.subtask_short: peer review for preprints and journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on peer-review practices that extend beyond traditional journal publication — including transparent review, reuse of referee reports, Review Commons refereed preprints, and editorial processes to improve fairness and scalability in life-science peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal manuscript evaluation and curation
rubrics_metrics.description: A central function of scientific journals is to evaluate and improve research manuscripts based on the advice of subject experts; ensure that the quality of the data presented and the claims made warrant inclusion in the scientific record; further curate data to ensure it is maximally accessible, conforms to ethical standards, and is presented in a manner that is in principle reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals apply editorial selection informed by expert advisors and peer reviewers. Quality assurance includes data accessibility, ethical conformity, and reproducibility. This curation adds value beyond basic peer review and supports retrieval and organization for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity for importance, relevance, and readership fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals (especially selective ones) evaluate manuscripts for importance, relevance and interest to their readership — in broad journals to facilitate exchange between domains, and in domain-specific journals to aggregate knowledge for retrieval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selectivity contributes to low acceptance rates and can create peer-review bottlenecks; editorial judgement about 'journal fit' is distinct from scientific quality and is an explicit part of journal assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent Peer Review (publish referee reports and author responses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of unedited referee reports alongside author responses and editorial decisions (confidential comments to the editors are not considered); editors sign their communication, but referees can opt to sign as they see fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public referee reports provide readers with viewpoints independent from authors, allow self‑training of referees, and enhance accountability. Transparent Review can be implemented on journal pages and extended to preprints (e.g., via TPiP/Hypothesis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-decision cross-referee commenting and moderated discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite referees to comment on each other's reports in an online discussion forum moderated by the editor—anonymously unless the referees signed their report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cross-comments aid editorial decisions, allow referees to recalibrate their assessment, reduce outlier opinions, and level the playing field between reviewers and authors. When major experimental revision is required, editors may engage in pre‑consultation with authors to invite their comments and a revision plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversify the referee pool and include early-career scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect diversification in the geographical and gender distribution of referee panels; include experienced early‑career scientists (ECRs) more systematically, for example for technical‑focused referee reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversification improves fairness and scalability of review. Co‑refereeing of mentors with named ECRs is encouraged. Progress towards equitable balance should be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse of constructive referee reports through transfer networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive referee reports are largely interoperable between journals and can be re-used; journal fit is an editorial matter and editors contextualize referee evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-using reviews via transfer networks (between related journals or partner presses) reduces serial review and reviewer depletion, shortens time to publication, and has shown high transfer success in specific partnerships (e.g., Life Science Alliance and partner presses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting referee reports alongside preprints (Refereed Preprints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post links to referee comments automatically on bioRxiv preprint versions of published papers, encourage authors to request posting on rejected manuscripts, and provide Refereed Preprints via platforms such as Review Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juxtaposing the evaluated manuscript with referee reports helps interpret evaluations, enhances training, showcases peer review value, increases visibility, and aids readers in assessing preprints. Posting is enabled via tools (e.g., TPiP/Hypothesis) and is at the authors' discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Commons: journal-independent high-quality peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide authors with a full set of quality referee reports independent of journal submission; accept manuscripts or preprints; authors can trigger posting of full reviews and responses alongside the preprint as a 'Refereed Preprint' and/or submit with those reports to partner journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliated journals may use Review Commons referee reports for decisions without restarting peer review. The service aims to reduce time spent re-submitting, relieve reviewer burden, promote objectivity (focus on science), and make reviews portable between journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote reviewer focus on scientific quality rather than journal fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracting the review process from the context of a specific journal encourages reviewers to concentrate on the science rather than specific journal fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review portability and journal‑independent reviews are posed to promote more objective assessments and allow reviewers to concentrate on scientific rigor and validity rather than suitability for one journal's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stably archived reviewed preprints as a dissemination end-point
rubrics_metrics.description: A stably archived preprint associated with reviews that provide context and quality assurance can be a reasonable end point in the scientific dissemination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While possible, community adoption may be gradual because current research assessment systems remain tied to venue; journals may support transitions as they occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-provided services not covered by reviewed preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals provide additional functions that reviewed preprints generally do not, including selective curation for interest and navigation, language editing and figure design, curation and quality control for data archiving and ethics, and broader visibility via summaries, reviews, press releases, and commentaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These services are reasons authors might still choose formal journal publication even when refereed preprints exist; editors should acknowledge which services they continue to provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author discretion and authentication of posted reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting of referee reports on preprints is at the discretion of the authors; referee reports made available via platforms are authenticated and can be used by journals for their editorial assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors choosing to post constructive reports on a preprint may attract other journals and provide confidence to readers; authentication of reports enables journals to rely on them instead of re‑reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce reviewer burden to canonical three reviews per manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to reduce peer review back to the canonical three per manuscript through reuse of reports and journal-independent review services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reducing per-manuscript reviewer counts is an explicit goal to relieve overburdened referees and improve scalability; transfer networks and Review Commons are mechanisms toward this aim.
